title: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
chiefComplaint: Crushing chest tightness like an elephant sitting on my chest, radiating down my left arm.

goldenQuestions.answer: The pain is right in the center of my breastbone and spreads heavily into my left arm and left jaw.
Yes, I broke out into a freezing cold sweat as soon as the pressure started.
It struck about 45 minutes ago while climbing the office staircase. Rest hasn't helped at all.
I have had diabetes and high blood pressure for 9 years and have smoked a pack a day since college.
I feel suffocated, like I cannot expand my lungs enough.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Pupils dilated secondary to acute sympathetic surge.

palpation.finding: Cold, clammy, pale extremities. Soft S4 gallop audible over cardiac apex. Bilateral lung bases clear.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Tachycardia at 108 bpm, S4 gallop present, no murmurs.

sourceCitation.title: AHA/ACC STEMI Clinical Practice Guidelines
sourceCitation.organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) / StatPearls

defaultResponse: Please help me doctor, this chest pressure is unbearable and my left arm feels numb and heavy.

title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (ADHF)
chiefComplaint: I cannot breathe when lying flat... I have to sleep sitting upright with three pillows.
trueDiagnosis: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure with Pulmonary Edema

goldenQuestions.answer: If I lie flat even for two minutes, I feel like I'm drowning. I've been sleeping propped up on 3 pillows.
My ankles and shins have swollen like balloons over the past four days. My slippers don't fit.
I have this constant bubbling cough that brings up pink, frothy fluid.
Yes, I wake up abruptly after 2 hours gasping and choking for air.
I attended a wedding 3 days ago and ate heavy salty feast food, and forgot my water pills.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Marked jugular venous distention (JVD) visible up to angle of mandible (JVP 8 cm).

palpation.finding: Bilateral 3+ pitting pedal edema up to mid-calf. Displaced hyperdynamic apical impulse.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Coarse bibasilar inspiratory crackles (rales) extending up to mid-lung zones with S3 gallop.

sourceCitation.title: Heart Failure: Evaluation and Management Guidelines
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: I can't... catch my breath... chest feels like it's filling with water...

title: Acute Pericarditis
chiefComplaint: Sharp chest pain that gets much worse when I lie down or breathe in, and feels better when I lean forward.

goldenQuestions.answer: When I lean forward sitting on the edge of the bed, the stabbing pain lessens. Lying flat is agonizing.
Taking a deep breath feels like a knife stabbing into my chest.
I had a bad viral flu with fever, runny nose, and body aches about a week ago.
The pain shoots up into my left trapezius shoulder ridge.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Anxious facies, sits leaning forward on exam table.

palpation.finding: No chest wall localized tenderness. Normal peripheral pulses.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: High-pitched superficial scratchy friction rub heard best at left sternal border during end-expiration.

sourceCitation.title: Acute Pericarditis: Pathophysiology and Practice
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: Doctor, whenever I try to lie flat, the sharp pain spikes immediately. Sitting forward helps.

title: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT)
chiefComplaint: My heart suddenly started racing at 180 beats a minute out of nowhere while drinking coffee.
urgentOrders: IV Adenosine 6 mg rapid push with saline flush

goldenQuestions.answer: It was like an on/off light switch! One second normal, next second racing like a hummingbird.
I pulled an all-nighter for exams and drank three large cold coffees this morning.
Yes, I felt lightheaded and my vision got blurry when it started pounding.
I had 2 similar racing episodes last year, but they stopped within 5 minutes after splashing cold water.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Normal ocular exam, anxious, flushed countenance.

palpation.finding: Rapid, regular peripheral pulses at 184 bpm. No peripheral edema.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Regular tachycardia at 184 bpm, no murmurs or extra heart sounds audible.

sourceCitation.title: Supraventricular Tachycardia Emergency Management
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: My heart is fluttering so fast in my throat, doctor! Please make it slow down.

title: Acute Infective Endocarditis
chiefComplaint: Spiking fevers, drenching night sweats, weight loss, and painless red spots on my palms for two weeks.
urgentOrders: 3 sets of Blood Cultures from separate venipuncture sites

goldenQuestions.answer: I noticed small flat, reddish painless spots on my palms and soles about five days ago.
Yes! I had a complex wisdom tooth extraction four weeks ago with significant bleeding.
A doctor told me years ago I had a mild bicuspid aortic valve murmur.
I have lost 6 kilograms over the past month and wake up drenched in sweat every single night.

pupilReflex.finding: Ophthalmoscopy reveals retinal hemorrhages with pale central spots (Roth Spots).

palpation.finding: Non-tender, erythematous macules on palms (Janeway Lesions). Splinter hemorrhages under fingernails.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: New-onset harsh early diastolic decrescendo murmur over right upper sternal border.

sourceCitation.title: Infective Endocarditis Duke Criteria & Practice Guide
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: I keep shivering with high fever every night, and these strange red spots appeared on my palms.

title: Acute Peritonsillar Abscess (Quinsy)
chiefComplaint: Severe one-sided throat agony, cannot swallow my own saliva, and my voice sounds muffled like a hot potato.
urgentOrders: Needle Aspiration / Incision and Drainage of Abscess

goldenQuestions.answer: I cannot swallow at all. It hurts so badly that I am drooling into a tissue cup.
I can barely open my jaw more than an inch. My jaw muscles feel completely locked.
(Speaks with muffled 'hot potato' resonance) Everyone tells me my voice sounds like I'm holding hot food in my mouth.
Yes, whenever I try to swallow, intense pain shoots directly into my right ear.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Examination of oropharynx reveals massive right tonsillar bulge with contralateral uvular deviation to the left.

palpation.finding: Severe trismus (interincisal distance <2 cm). Tender, enlarged right anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Normal vesicular breath sounds, no inspiratory stridor.

sourceCitation.title: Peritonsillar Abscess: Emergency Drainage and Care
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: (Muffled speech) Doctor, my right throat is swollen shut... I can't even swallow my own spit.

title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
chiefComplaint: The entire room spins violently for 30 seconds whenever I turn my head over in bed to the right.
urgentOrders: Assess HINTS exam to rule out central cerebellar stroke

goldenQuestions.answer: The intense spinning lasts only about 20 to 30 seconds, then calms down as long as I keep my head perfectly still.
It happens exclusively when I roll over onto my right side in bed or tilt my head up to look at a high shelf.
No hearing loss, no ringing, and no ear fullness whatsoever.
No facial drooping, no arm weakness, and no slurred speech.

pupilReflex.finding: Dix-Hallpike maneuver on right side elicits classic torsional upbeating nystagmus after a 4-second latency, resolving within 25 seconds.

palpation.finding: Normal cranial nerves II-XII. No cerebellar dysmetria on finger-to-nose testing.

sourceCitation.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Assessment & Epley Maneuver
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: When I turn my head, doctor, the walls and ceiling spin around me uncontrollably.

title: Acute Mastoiditis
chiefComplaint: Throbbing ear agony, high fever, and my ear is visibly sticking outwards with red swelling behind it.
urgentOrders: Contrast-Enhanced High-Resolution CT of Temporal Bones
Urgent ENT Surgical Consultation for Myringotomy / Tympanocentesis

goldenQuestions.answer: The bone right behind my left ear is red, hot, swollen, and feels like a throbbing toothache.
I had a severe middle ear infection 10 days ago. I took antibiotics for only 3 days and stopped when it felt slightly better.
Pus has been intermittently oozing out of my left ear canal.
My left ear hearing is completely muffled and feels clogged with water.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Examination behind left ear shows postauricular erythema, loss of retroauricular crease, and anterior displacement of auricle.

palpation.finding: Intense tenderness and boggy fluctuation over the left mastoid process. Otoscopy reveals bulging, erythematous left tympanic membrane with purulent otorrhea.

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Lungs clear bilaterally, febrile tachycardia present.

sourceCitation.title: Mastoiditis: Diagnosis and Surgical Intervention Protocols
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: The bone behind my left ear is throbbing with pain, and my ear is visibly sticking forward.

title: Acute Adult Epiglottitis (Airway Emergency)
chiefComplaint: Rapidly worsening severe throat pain, inability to swallow saliva, and leaning forward in a tripod position to breathe.
urgentOrders: IMMEDIATE AIRWAY PREPARATION: Anesthesia & ENT on standby for fiberoptic intubation / cricothyroidotomy
DO NOT perform forceful tongue depressor exam
Urgent Portable Lateral Soft Tissue Neck Radiograph ('Thumbprint sign')

goldenQuestions.answer: Swallowing feels like swallowing razor blades. I am drooling into a cup because I can't swallow my spit.
I have to lean forward with my hands on my knees to keep my airway open. Lying back makes me feel like I am choking to death.
My voice is muffled and hoarse, and every breath produces a quiet raspy wheeze.
It developed frighteningly fast—I was completely healthy this morning and by 3 PM I was gasping.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Patient is in acute distress in 'tripod' posture (sitting upright, leaning forward, neck hyperextended, drooling).

palpation.finding: Gentle palpation of larynx/hyoid elicits marked tenderness. Pharynx appears deceptively normal on gentle inspection (infection is supraglottic).
palpation.sign: Tripod Posture & Pain Out of Proportion to Pharyngeal Exam

physicalExam.chestAuscultation: Inspiratory stridor audible over anterior neck with tachypnea.

sourceCitation.title: Epiglottitis: Emergency Airway Management Guidelines
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: (Struggling to speak) Throat... on fire... can't swallow... airway closing...

title: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss (SSNHL)
chiefComplaint: I woke up this morning and my right ear was suddenly 90% deaf with loud ringing, like someone flipped an audio switch.
urgentOrders: Emergent Pure Tone Audiometry (PTA within 24 hours)
High-Dose Oral Prednisolone (60 mg/day taper) within 72 hours
Otoscopic Exam (Exclude cerumen or middle ear effusion)
Gadolinium-Enhanced MRI of Brain & Internal Auditory Canal

goldenQuestions.answer: It happened overnight. I woke up at 6:30 AM, picked up my phone, put it to my right ear, and heard complete dead static.
Yes! There is a high-pitched loud buzzing ringing noise constantly screaming in that ear.
Mild unsteadiness when walking, but no spinning vertigo.
No pain, no ear discharge, and no earwax history. The ear canal feels completely empty but deaf.

pupilReflex.finding: PERRLA. Normal ocular and facial symmetry. Cranial nerves VII normal.

palpation.finding: Otoscopy shows completely clear, pearly grey tympanic membrane bilaterally. Weber tuning fork test (512 Hz) lateralizes to the normal left ear. Rinne test positive (AC > BC bilaterally).
palpation.sign: Weber Lateralization to Normal Ear (Sensorineural Pattern)

sourceCitation.title: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss Practice Guideline
sourceCitation.organization: NCBI Bookshelf / National Institutes of Health

defaultResponse: Doctor, my right ear went almost completely deaf overnight and has a loud high-pitched buzz.
